question: Should OpenClaw adopt aggregate recovery-point, final-handoff, and restored-admission contracts as normative extensions of RFC 0013, or keep scale-to-zero lifecycle design in a separate owner-sponsored direction?
rationale: The patch is documentation-only, but it establishes new fail-closed lifecycle and compatibility expectations that implementation review cannot resolve without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor the sidecar direction
options.body: Accept the host-neutral contract boundary, then review the wording and implementation trackers as the path for future host integrations.

options.title: Keep RFC 0013 narrow
options.body: Leave the completed SQLite artifact RFC unchanged and pursue any lifecycle contract only through a separately sponsored RFC or canonical product tracker.

options.title: Request a narrower addendum
options.body: Retain only the noncontroversial responsibility split and defer normative handoff and admission semantics until their owning implementation path is approved.

recommendation.title: Keep RFC 0013 narrow
recommendation.body: Leave the completed SQLite artifact RFC unchanged and pursue any lifecycle contract only through a separately sponsored RFC or canonical product tracker.

likelyOwner.reason: The proposal explicitly composes the existing snapshot and cooperative-suspension contracts associated with this area.
